This is mitigated by TPMs having endorsement keys and certificates, which can be verified by a list of legitimate vendors and their CA keys. One of the most notable is the use of [[nodiscard]] to indicate that a function or variable should not be used after it is no longer needed, which has been a game-changer for fixing bugs and improving code readability. Additionally, the use of [[maybe_unused]] to indicate that a variable should not be used after it is no longer needed has been a useful pattern. These conventions have also led to the elimination of unused variables and improved code organization, making it easier to maintain and debug code.

articles.title: JPEG XL vs AVIF for web use-cases
articles.summary: JPEG XL vs AVIF for web use-cases has now landed in all major browsers, and its performance varies depending on the use-case. At default effort settings, AVIF almost always produces smaller files than JPEG XL, but at maximum effort settings, the gap narrows to typically 6-20%. AVIF is faster to encode and decode, and uses less memory, but its files are typically larger, and its performance is better on balance.
